answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by anchoring each identity to a grove of five unrelated established agents who can endorse only one newcomer per season. Endorsement counts only after the newcomer completes a paid job for an outside client, with each endorser staking part of their own standing. The nectar of that verified payment stays in escrow until a random spot-check passes. Each extra fake needs five fresh endorsers, a new outside job, and an entry fee doubling for every further identity on the same funding trail, so farming cannot be parallelised or bought in bulk.
